strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy accuracy bug in `scipy.interpolate.RectBivariateSpline` where, for large 2D inputs and any smoothing `s>0`, the evaluated spline intermittently (most of the time) becomes NaN everywhere; the added regression test (`test_spline_large_2d` in `test_fitpack2.py`) should fail on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed one.

pip_packages: pythran (optional; not required for this test)
build_commands: pip install -e .  # will be replaced with an editable install from the target SciPy revision
pinned_because: SciPy and NumPy versions are explicitly part of the documented reproduction environment for this bug: SciPy 1.9.3 with NumPy 1.23.5 (and alternative SciPy 1.10.0/NumPy 1.24.1 exists, but this plan targets the explicitly documented pair).
This test targets `RectBivariateSpline` behavior in SciPy’s FITPACK wrappers, so building SciPy from source at the exact buggy commit and fixed commit is required to guarantee the transition.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy SciPy revision (commit `a65c459ea933`), `test_spline_large_2d` fails because `assert(not np.isnan(z_spl).any())` is violated (i.e., `z_spl` contains NaNs). On the fixed revision, the same test passes: `z_spl` contains no NaNs and `xp_assert_close(z_spl, z, atol=..., rtol=...)` succeeds for each parametrized (shape, s).
strategy.numerical_probe: The transition is decided by the test’s NaN check: `assert(not np.isnan(z_spl).any())` after `z_spl = spl(x, y)` for large `(nx, ny)` and `s in {1,3}` (also `s=0` as a control).

input_output_examples.input: s=1; shape=(1000,1700) (used by separate `test_spline_large_2d_maxit`), x=np.arange(nx), y=np.arange(ny), z=rng.integers(0,100,(nx,ny)).astype(np.float64), spl=RectBivariateSpline(x,y,z,s=s), z_spl=spl(x,y), check `np.isnan(z_spl).any()`
input_output_examples.buggy_output: True (NaNs appear; reported as NaN everywhere)

input_output_examples.input: shape=(350,850) or (2000,170); parameters over s_tols: (0,1e-12,1e-7), (1,7e-3,1e-4), (3,2e-2,1e-4); generate x=np.arange(nx), y=np.arange(ny), z=rng.integers(0,100,(nx,ny)).astype(np.float64); spl=RectBivariateSpline(x,y,z,s=s); z_spl=spl(x,y); check `not np.isnan(z_spl).any()`

risks: This bug is described as irregular (may sometimes work, most of the time it does not). CI timing/BLAS/CPU characteristics may affect the frequency of failure; if it does not fail on first run, re-run the same test process multiple times to capture the intermittent failure.
The test is marked `@pytest.mark.slow()` but should still run; ensure you do not use `-m
If you instead run on 32-bit platforms, there is an explicit `skipif` for the `maxit`-focused test; while `test_spline_large_2d` is not skipped, platform differences can still change behavior.
This plan pins NumPy to 1.23.5 and Python 3.10.8 as explicitly documented; the PR also mentions an alternative environment (NumPy 1.24.1/SciPy 1.10.0) but success may differ there.

oracle.reference_source: Regression test oracle in SciPy: `assert(not np.isnan(z_spl).any())` and `xp_assert_close(z_spl, z, atol=..., rtol=...)` inside `test_spline_large_2d` (for each parametrized s/shape).
oracle.why: The transition is based on the test’s internal assertions, especially the NaN predicate; no external numerical values need to be inspected beyond the test checks.

fails_on_buggy.description: what the assertion sees on the buggy revision, and why that makes it fail

passes_on_fixed.description: what happens on the fixed revision
